name: Mount Everett
generated_description:
Mount Everett is a 2,602-foot summit in Massachusetts. The Mount Everett Trail covers 1.3 miles round trip (out-and-back) with about 105 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

The Route

Along the way the route passes a rest area (Guilder Pond Picnic area) near mile 0 — useful checkpoints for judging your pace.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 42.10823, -73.43491 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 40 miles southeast of Albany, New York. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Spring through fall is the main season. Conditions change fast in the shoulder months — check a point forecast for the summit, not the nearest town, before you commit.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Mount Race, Alander Mountain and Mount Frissell — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.question: How long does it take to hike Mount Everett?
faqs.answer: The Mount Everett Trail is 1.3 miles round trip with about 105 feet of elevation gain, and most hikers take roughly 0.5 hours of moving time. Add time for breaks and conditions — winter or wet weather can double the trip.

faqs.question: How hard is the Mount Everett hike?
faqs.answer: It's rated Easy using the National Park Service difficulty formula (1.3 miles round trip, 105 ft of gain — about 100 ft of climbing per mile). The elevation profile on this page shows exactly where the steep sections fall.

faqs.question: Where is the Mount Everett trailhead?
faqs.answer: The trailhead is at 42.10823, -73.43491 in Massachusetts. Use the driving-directions link in the Getting There section above, and note that parking at popular trailheads fills early on weekends.

faqs.question: Are dogs allowed on the Mount Everett trail?
faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.question: When is the best time to hike Mount Everett?
faqs.answer: Late May through October for snow-free hiking. Check a summit point forecast before you go — conditions up high differ from the trailhead.

faqs.question: How tall is Mount Everett?
faqs.answer: Mount Everett stands at 2,602 feet (793 meters) in Massachusetts.
